ambiguities_declared: The controlled relation vocabulary has no phrase specific to reporting deadlines; the 10-day reporting requirements (c1, c4) were classified as 'requires-monitoring' as the closest fit rather than a guessed new relation.

The recordkeeping/retention requirement in 141.629(b) does not cleanly match any controlled relation phrase; it was classified as 'compliance-basis' rather than left uncaptured, but this is an approximation.

This section references § 141.64(b)(2), § 141.625, and § 141.33 for substantive definitions and requirements (violation determination, increased monitoring, and record retention specifics) that cannot be resolved from this section's text alone.
'Operational evaluation levels' (141.629(a)(1)(v)) is referenced but not defined within this section.

challenge_questions.question: How many days after the end of a quarter must a system report Stage 2 DBPR (TTHM/HAA5) monitoring results to the State?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: It is the arithmetic average of quarterly TTHM/HAA5 results for the last four quarters at that monitoring location.
challenge_questions.question: How is the LRAA (locational running annual average) calculated at each monitoring location?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: Whether the running annual average (RAA) exceeded 4.0 mg/L.
challenge_questions.question: What source water TOC RAA value is relevant to whether a subpart H system stays eligible for reduced TTHM/HAA5 monitoring?
Who has the option to perform the MCL/reduced-monitoring compliance calculations instead of the system reporting them?

challenge_questions.expected_answer: Subpart V monitoring plans and monitoring results, retained as required by § 141.33.
challenge_questions.question: What must a system retain under the recordkeeping provision of this section, and per which cross-referenced section?

verified_quotes.exact_text: (a) Reporting. (1) You must report the following information for each monitoring location to the State within 10 days of the end of any quarter in which monitoring is required:

(iii) Arithmetic average of quarterly results for the last four quarters for each monitoring location (LRAA), beginning at the end of the fourth calendar quarter that follows the compliance date and at the end of each subsequent quarter. If the LRAA calculated based on fewer than four quarters of data would cause the MCL to be exceeded regardless of the monitoring results of subsequent quarters, you must report this information to the State as part of the first report due following the compliance date or anytime thereafter that this determination is made. If you are required to conduct monitoring at a frequency that is less than quarterly, you must make compliance calculations beginning with the first compliance sample taken after the compliance date, unless you are required to conduct increased monitoring under § 141.625.
(iv) Whether, based on § 141.64(b)(2) and this subpart, the MCL was violated at any monitoring location.
(v) Any operational evaluation levels that were exceeded during the quarter and, if so, the location and date, and the calculated TTHM and HAA5 levels.

(2) If you are a subpart H system seeking to qualify for or remain on reduced TTHM/HAA5 monitoring, you must report the following source water TOC information for each treatment plant that treats surface water or ground water under the direct influence of surface water to the State within 10 days of the end of any quarter in which monitoring is required:
(iv) The running annual average (RAA) of quarterly averages from the past four quarters.
(3) The State may choose to perform calculations and determine whether the MCL was exceeded or the system is eligible for reduced monitoring in lieu of having the system report that information
(b) Recordkeeping. You must retain any subpart V monitoring plans and your subpart V monitoring results as required by § 141.33.
